## Which channel earned a conversion?

Switch among five ways to split the 3,020 conversions in tracked journeys, then select a channel to inspect. The blue bars are **attribution credit** from the observed paths. Green bars are the seeded generator's counterfactual result: conversions lost if that channel had not reached its users, keeping the other channels and random draws fixed. The totals differ because a journey-credit budget must sum to tracked conversions, while channel effects can overlap.

**Work one example.** Last click assigns retargeting 1,114 conversions, more than any other channel. Removing it in the synthetic counterfactual loses zero conversions. It reaches high-intent users late, so the path records it even when it caused nothing. A budget decision needs a holdout or lift test, not a more elaborate way to count touches.

**Data.** [Seeded synthetic journeys](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/mta_journeys.csv) and [known counterfactual truth](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/truth_mta.json). The [module](../modules/16-multi-touch-attribution.qmd) computes all five credit methods on those journeys. These are measured results of that simulation, not evidence that one attribution method always ranks better.
